data.title: Cyber-attackers slammed the brakes on Jaguar Land Rover's manufacturing
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 2025年9月，捷豹路虎遭遇严重网络攻击，导致其全球工厂停产，每天损失约7200万英镑销售额。这次危机发生在公司电动车型推出延迟、特朗普关税政策冲击的困难时期，可能导致120亿英镑利润损失。停产已影响20万供应链就业，部分工人被迫申请政府救济。文章呼吁英国政府效仿疫情期间的援助措施，为供应链提供紧急财政支持，避免重蹈2005年MG Rover倒闭后的覆辙，并批评当前缺乏区域性产业政策。商业贸易部被敦促采取行动而非仅观望局势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Jaguar Land Rover（JLR）遭受网络攻击后的生产中断、供应链影响、网络安全措施及政府援助。

不同观点：
• **对JLR网络安全的批评**  
  许多评论指出JLR的网络安全措施不足，尤其是将网络安全外包给第三方公司，导致漏洞频发。例如，有用户提到JLR的IT系统老旧，缺乏内部专业团队，外包模式难以应对复杂攻击。

• **政府援助的争议**  
  部分用户支持英国政府提供15亿英镑贷款，认为这是保护就业和供应链的必要举措。但也有反对声音，认为这是用纳税人的钱为企业的疏忽买单，质疑JLR是否应自行承担风险。

• **供应链脆弱性的讨论**  
  有评论强调此次攻击暴露了汽车行业供应链的脆弱性，尤其是对Just-in-Time（JIT）生产模式的依赖。攻击导致3万辆汽车减产，引发对全球供应链弹性的担忧。

• **对恢复时间的悲观预期**  
  一些用户对JLR快速恢复生产持悲观态度，认为“没人知道”何时能复工，反映了网络攻击对实体经济的长期影响。也有观点认为JLR可能借此机会升级系统，但代价高昂。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：政府援助是否合理，以及JLR是否应优先投资网络安全而非事后补救。  
• **行业影响**：讨论扩展到其他车企是否面临类似风险，以及是否需要行业-wide的网络安全标准。

45468621.article_content:
September 22, 2025
The GIST
Cyber-attackers slammed the brakes on Jaguar Land Rover's manufacturing. Why the UK government should step in
by David Bailey,
The Conversation
edited by
Lisa Lock
, 																								reviewed by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
written by researcher(s)
proofread
Credit: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain
Car manufacturing at Jaguar Land Rover recently ground to a halt after a "
catastrophic
" cyber-attack.
Forced to shut down plants in the UK, Slovakia, Brazil, India and China, the disruption comes at a challenging time for the company. It had already
postponed the launch
of new models after the uptake of electric vehicles stalled. And Donald Trump's
tariffs
have been a major cause of concern for the British car industry as a whole.
Profits at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) will undoubtedly take a hit, as they did at
M&S
and
Co-op
when they were the victims of
cyber-attacks
earlier this year.
Normally, JLR makes around
1,000 cars a day
, with the average price of a new vehicle around £72,000. That means JLR is missing out on daily sales of some £72 million, and profits of £5 million a day.
The firm has now
extended the shutdown
to September 24 2025, by which time the loss of revenues will be around £1.7 billion and the hit to profits some £120 million. There are even fears that this
could go on until November
, and restarting production will be a complex business given the "build to order" nature of premium cars (when vehicles are only manufactured after a customer purchase is confirmed).
But the longer the shutdown goes on, the more likely it is that those customers will simply decide to go elsewhere. For the time being,
spare parts
can't be ordered, cars can't be serviced, and new car sales will stall, in what is usually a particularly busy month.
The firm's brand image will take a battering too, to add to recent social media derision which has included an attack
from Donald Trump
and a much
maligned brand relaunch
last year which centered on the controversial design of its
"Type OO"
concept car.
There are also livelihoods at stake. The company's
supply chain
, centered in the west Midlands region of the UK, supports as many as
200,000 jobs
.
The longer the shutdown goes on the bigger the
impact on the supply chain
. Firms have already sent staff home, while others are running out of money. According to the Unite union, some supply chain workers have been told to
apply for state benefits
.
Road ahead
For its part, JLR has said that it can survive the
shutdown
but that its supply chain will need help—a call echoed by
the union
and
some members of parliament
.
And the UK government really needs to start thinking about a
financial lifeline
to keep the supply chain going. That could be in the form of a furlough scheme to keep workers in place or some sort of loan scheme for supply chain firms.
Both were used
during COVID
and thought to have safeguarded some 4 million jobs.
Emergency support in response to shocks is common in other countries like
Germany
, and has been used in the UK car manufacturing supply chain before, after the
MG Rover closure
in 2005, and also after the 2011 Japanese earthquake and tsunami which saw the interrupted flow of key components from Japan
shut down production
at Honda.
That support came via the regional development agency Advantage West Midlands (in the case of MG Rover) and later the Manufacturing Advisory Service (after the Japanese earthquake).
Both agencies have since been scrapped, underscoring the lack of any "place-based" or region-specific
industrial policy
capacity in England. That really needs to change.
The Department for Business and Trade and its new secretary of state Peter Kyle need to be doing more than
just monitoring the situation
. It needs to start thinking about how emergency support could be
provided to the supply chain
. A huge number of jobs depend on JLR getting up and running again—and quickly.

data.title: Babel is why I keep blogging with Emacs
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 作者羡慕他人简单的静态博客生成工具，希望自己开发一个2000行代码的博客引擎，但实际使用的是Org模式发布文章。虽然Org模式依赖复杂的Lisp代码框架（超2万行）且难以理解，但其Babel功能能运行并嵌入代码输出（如表格、图像），支持多语言交互，尤其适合R绘图，使他无法放弃。因此，尽管简化方案诱人，他仍选择忍受Org模式的复杂性以保留Babel的强大功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[博客写作工具的选择与自动化程度之间的权衡]

不同观点：
• **akkartik**：倾向于手动工具以获得更多控制和灵活性，尤其是对于需要生成动态或交互式内容的情况。
• **thecsw**：虽然最初使用复杂的工具链，但最终选择自己编写简单的静态网站生成器以获得完全的控制和理解。
• **ashton314**：使用Hugo和ox-hugo的组合，因为org-mode已经是他日常工作的一部分，工具链的集成性更重要。
• **ineedasername**：建议在自定义工具中集成部分现有工具（如Babel）的功能，以平衡控制和便利性。
• **siavosh**：寻求最简单、零JavaScript的博客发布方案，强调极简主义和自动化。
• **cosmic_quanta**：使用Pandoc和自定义工具（如pandoc-plot）来处理技术文档中的图表生成。
• **whacked_new**：虽然org-mode和Babel功能强大，但市场更倾向于Markdown，且类似功能可以移植到Markdown。
• **facundo_olano**：自己编写轻量级的org-mode静态生成器，避免复杂工具的依赖。
• **NeutralForest**：从org-mode转向Markdown和Zola，认为简单性比功能更重要。
• **ks2048**：认为格式应独立于编辑器，避免被特定工具（如Emacs）限制。
• **SoftTalker**：几乎所有写作都在Emacs中完成，但对某些工具（如Teams）的支持不足。
• **piker**：使用自定义工具（Tritium）来发布博客，强调工具的迭代和改进。
• **m-hodges**：赞赏Quarto的代码执行和输出嵌入功能，类似于Babel。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否应该使用现成的工具链（如Hugo、org-mode）还是自己编写工具？支持现成工具的一方强调集成性和社区支持，而支持自定义工具的一方则强调控制和灵活性。
• **工具链的复杂性**：许多用户提到从复杂工具转向简单工具的经历，反映了对工具链复杂性的不同容忍度。
• **市场趋势**：Markdown因其简单性和广泛支持而成为主流，但org-mode和Babel在某些场景（如技术写作）中仍有不可替代的优势。

45453222.article_content:
Every time I look at someone’s simple static site generation setup for their
blog, I feel a pang of envy. I’m sure I could make a decent blogging engine in
2,000 lines of code, and it would be something I’d understand, be proud over,
able to extend, and willing to share with others.
Instead, I write these articles in Org mode, and use mostly the standard Org
publishing functions to export them to
html
. This is
sometimes brittle
, but
most annoyingly, I don’t understand it. I have been asked for details on how my
publishing flow works, but the truth is I have no idea what happens when I run
the
org-publish-current-file
command.
I could find out by tracing the evaluation of the Lisp code that runs on export,
but I won’t, because just the
html
exporting code (
ox-html.el
) is 5,000
lines of complexity. The general exporting framework (
ox-publish.el
and
ox.el
) is 8,000 lines. The framework depends on Org parsing code
(
org-element.el
) which is at least another 9,000 lines. This is over 20,000
lines of complexity I’d need to contend with.
It might seem like a no-brainer to just write that 2,000 line custom static
generator and use that instead.
Except one thing: Babel.
Any lightweight markup format (like Markdown or ReStructuredText or whatever)
allows for embedding code blocks, but Org, through Babel, can
run
that code on
export, and then display the output in the published document,
even when the
output is a table or an image
. It supports sessions that lets code reuse
definitions from earlier code blocks. It allows for injecting variables from the
markup into the code, and vice versa. As a bonus, Org doesn’t require a
JavaScript syntax highlighter, because it generates inline styles in the source
code.
It does this for a large number of languages, although I mainly use it with R
for drawing plots. Being able to do this is incredibly convenient, because it
makes it trivial to
draft data, illustrations, and text at the same time
,
adjusting both until the article coheres. Having tried it, I cannot see myself
living without it.
A simple 2,000 line blogging engine would be a fun weekend project. Mirroring
the features of Babel I use would turn it into a multi-month endeavour for
someone with limited time such as myself. Not going to happen, and I will
continue to beat myself up for overcomplicating my publishing workflow.
